newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia stocks end mixed, Bavaria gains.
newsitem.headline: Colombia stocks end mixed, Bavaria gains.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended mixed in see-saw trading that saw brewer Bavaria and cement maker Cementos Argos among the day's few big winners.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index rose 1.23 percent to close at 14,975.79 on a below-average volume of 936.8 million pesos. Bogota's IBB slipped 0.08 percent ending at 965.73. Volume in Bogota was 1.7 billion pesos.

Traders said foreign fund buying of Bavaria pushed it up 3.86 percent to 6,050 pesos per share in Medellin. The brewer also accounted for a bulk of the volume in Bogota, but its gain in the capital was a slightly lower 3.26 percent.
"There was a lot of activity involving Bavaria," one Bogota-based broker said. "The stock is very strong now thanks to expectations of good (Q4) results," he said.

Cementos Argos, the day's other big gainer, closed up 3.58 percent in Bogota and up 3.65 percent in Medellin in moves that brokers attributed to hopes of a near-term pickup in Colombia's depressed construction sector. Cementos Caribe, which belongs like Argos to the powerful Sindicato Antioqueo conglomerate, rose 1.20 percent in Medellin to close at 5,060 per share. Suramericanas de Seguros, another Sindicato holding, fell 11 percent on in Bogota, however.

Bogota stock exchange president Carlos Caballero said investment activity in stocks had fallen 60 percent last week amid widespread uncertainty stemming from the government's recently announced package of economic emergency measures.
But activity could pick up next week, since Caballero told a news conference the government had agreed to back-track on one measure that was potentially devastating for stocks.
The government had announced last week that stock market earnings would no longer be considered tax exempt. Caballero said it agreed Friday to maintain the exemption for all investment in equities.
